title: Multi-tenant session attribution dimensional model for Console analytics
creator: Priya Desai
description: Design and implement a multi-tenant, session-level dimensional model to replace ad-hoc event rollups used by the Console dashboards. Current problems: inconsistent session attribution across routes, heavy realtime joins in Metabase queries, and difficulty tracking feature enablement entitlements over time. This ticket covers the canonical schema (session_dim, event_fact, entitlement_dim, workspace_dim), partitioning strategy, SCD handling for workspace/entitlement attributes, and ETL contract for upstream producers (backend services + edge ingestion).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical session_dim table created with stable primary key (session_id) and tenant scoping (workspace_id) and is populated nightly
Event_fact table contains pre-computed session attribution fields (session_id, session_start_ts, session_end_ts, route_sequence, dominant_route) to avoid expensive joins in dashboard queries
Workspace_dim implements SCD2 for org/plan/region attributes and has end_date/start_date columns for time-travel queries
Entitlement_dim captures per-workspace feature flags with effective_from/effective_to and is joinable to event_fact and session_dim
Query examples in Console dashboards run under 30s on production-sized partitions and are covered by unit tests
Backfill plan and stop-gap views provided so Console dashboards are not disrupted during rollout
implementation_plan: 1) Finalize schema and column naming with analytics and Console PMs
2) Add upstream contract change: producers include a stable session_id in the ingestion envelope (edge + backend) and emit 'session_boundary' events
3) Build nightly Spark job to assemble session_dim from session_boundary + activity streams with per-tenant watermarking
4) Create event_fact transform that enriches raw events with session_id, workspace attributes (joined to last-known workspace_dim), and entitlement snapshot at event_ts
5) Implement SCD2 loader for workspace_dim and entitlement_dim using source-of-truth from Billing/Accounts service
6) Create partitioning scheme (dt=event_date, workspace_id hash bucketing) and add high-level access-control tags for Private deployments
7) Run validation and perf tests, then backfill 90 days of historical sessions for pilot orgs
8) Coordinate deployment with Console frontend to switch to new endpoints/views
migration_strategy: Deploy transforms to the curated layer as new table names (session_dim_v1, event_fact_v1). Keep legacy rollup views in place. Run dual-population for 2 weeks: populate both legacy and new tables, compare row counts and aggregation results nightly using a validation DAG. Once parity and perf targets met, cut over dashboards to the new tables and retire legacy views after 1 week of monitoring.
sql_examples:
-- Example: reconstruct a session by windowing session_boundary events
CREATE TABLE curated.session_dim_v1 AS
SELECT
  session_id,
  workspace_id,
  MIN(ts) AS session_start_ts,
  MAX(ts) AS session_end_ts,
  COUNT(*) AS event_count,
  HASH_MOD(FNV_HASH(workspace_id), 32) AS workspace_bucket,
  current_workspace_plan AS plan,
  current_region as region
FROM raw.console_events
WHERE event_type IN ('session_boundary','route_change','route_ping')
GROUP BY session_id, workspace_id;
notes: Key trade-off: keeping session assembly nightly reduces realtime cost but introduces up to 15m freshness SLA — acceptable for billing and long-term attribution but not for live debugging. Consider a small realtime cache for critical route latency charts
We will use hashed workspace bucketing to avoid small files and achieve even partition distribution across partitions
Workspace SCD source is the Accounts API; entitlement snapshots are pulled from the Feature Flagging service and joined by workspace_id / effective_ts
